questions.prompt: An ISR updates a volatile long count. On an 8-bit AVR, what must loop() do to read it safely?
options: Nothing: volatile already makes the read atomic.
Call delay(1) first so the ISR can finish.
Read it twice and keep the larger value.
Copy it between noInterrupts() and interrupts().
questions.explanation: A 4-byte read takes several instructions and the ISR can run between them; copy it with interrupts disabled.

questions.prompt: Uno Timer1 in CTC mode, 16 MHz, prescaler 8, target interrupt rate 2 kHz. What OCR1A value?
A quadrature decoder (x4) receives the (A,B) samples 00, 10, 11, 01, 00, 10 with A leading B being forward. What is the net count?
Why is a 50 ms time-window debounce a poor way to read an encoder?
options: The window costs too much memory.
Genuine edges come faster than 50 ms and would be thrown away.
Encoders never bounce, so debouncing is unnecessary.
Debouncing is only allowed inside an ISR.
questions.explanation: At speed the genuine edges are closer together than the window, so real counts would be discarded; a state table cancels bounce without a window.

questions.prompt: An encoder ISR takes 10 us and fires 25 000 times per second. What fraction of the CPU does it use, in percent?
Which statement is acceptable inside an Arduino ISR?
questions.explanation: Incrementing a volatile counter is a few instructions. Serial.print, delay and String allocation all block or allocate.

questions.prompt: Two encoders on an ESP32 each produce 90 000 edges per second. Explain how you would count them reliably and what you must still check.
rubric: Computes the interrupt load (180 000 edges/s times the ISR time) and shows it is too high.
Uses the hardware pulse counter (PCNT) in quadrature mode, with its glitch filter, and reads it at a modest rate.
Handles the counter range or overflow and reads atomically, and validates against a known move.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
